Why do upvotes lag on Voat, but appear instantly on reddit?
Voat doesn't own it's servers. Reddit does.

Good point, but reddit is also under heavy traffic pretty much everyday. I'm wondering what they do differently than Voat to make upvotes appear so quickly, even during peak traffic times. I'm thinking maybe the upvote isn't registered right away, but it makes users think it is, whereas Voat is more "real time" with its upvotes, if that makes sense.
/v/diodine answered this perfectly up above -- it's a design decision that Voat could also make.

Because on Reddit when you vote JavaScript instantly changes the color of the button while asynchronously sending a message to the Reddit server that you cast a vote.

On Voat it sends the message to the server and waits for the response and changes the button color based on the result.

Voat is slower but more accurate to what the server is doing.

Reddit is faster but the vote color does not accurately represent what your cast vote is.

Thanks for the technically accurate answer. This design decision has nothing to do with the language or included libraries in said language, and everything to do with choosing to make a UI which appears completely responsive and hides its overhead from the user vs. a UI which moves at the pace of its overhead.

Personally I like the former better for an OS, but for a web app, the latter.
